identity: Utrecht University, Dutch-taught Artificial Intelligence (Kunstmatige Intelligentie) bachelor, 2026–27

sources.scope: Utrecht public degree overview. Confirms the interdisciplinary focus on technological, philosophical, linguistic and psychological aspects of AI.
Official programme overview and teaching descriptions. First-year Dutch instruction, four teaching blocks and three named depth packages.
Official student curriculum for current cohorts, sequencing and credits.
Official descriptions of Learning and Computation, Reasoning and Computation and Cognitive Processing.
2026–2027 programme-specific OER, Articles 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, footnote 1 and Appendices 1–2. Controls identity, compulsory courses, levels, choices and graduation research.
Official work and postgraduate examples, used for search context.
Official thesis guidance. Separate preparation, one-block standard and two-block expanded variants, individual proposal and supervised writing.
Official course planner for Learning and Computation and bound choices. Confirms slots A, B and C for the illustrated Period 1 depth courses.

Official 2026–27 Course Planner for KI3V12011. Individual research and written thesis, four mandatory class meetings, four possible starts and 7.5 EC charged to profiling for the expanded version. No entry-credit threshold specified here.
Official profiling requirements: 45 EC, at least 15 at level 2 or 3, no master’s courses. Minor, electives, second package, approved external study or internship up to 15 EC.

curriculum: The 2026–2027 full-time programme is predominantly Dutch, with English allowed for up to a third of teaching under Article 3.3. The standard 180 EC plan is 60 EC in two compulsory basic packages, 15 EC disciplinary requirements, a single 45 EC depth package, 7.5 EC of experimental methods, 7.5 EC individual thesis, and 45 EC of profiling space. The first-listed Learning and Computation package is selected without reference to UCR fit. Its four fixed courses and one course from each of groups B and C appear exactly once. The first eligible choices are Logic for AI II and Experimental Psycholinguistics. The five level-3 depth courses supply 37.5 EC, plus 7.5 each for Language Models, experimental methods and thesis, or 60 advanced EC, over the 45 EC major minimum. At least 15 EC of profiling is level 2 or 3. The programme coordinator may approve a 15 EC thesis using 7.5 EC of that profiling space. The comparison uses the standard 7.5 EC version.
progression: Year 1 foundations introduce logic, cognition, mathematics and programming before formal languages, nature-inspired computation, language models and introductory machine learning. The disciplinary and depth courses follow the foundations. The three Period 1 depth examples can be spread over Years 2 and 3, leaving space for the compulsory Period 1 algorithms course. The depth choices are at distinct published slots. The standard thesis is supervised and completed in one block, with the research plan submitted in Week 3. The illustrative route places experimental methods in Year 3 Block 3 and the standard thesis in Block 4, which follows the published preparation guidance. The course planner gives four possible starting blocks and lists no fixed completed-credit threshold. No threshold from the separate Liberal Arts and Sciences route is imported.
components: Utrecht requires a supervised thesis after preparation in experimental methods. UCR offers optional independent research outside these schedules.
Utrecht leaves 45 EC for profiling, such as a minor or electives, subject to programme requirements.
